engine: A building shown у розрізі as BIG renders side by side: N vertical slabs, one open at a time. At rest each slab is a narrow STRIP with a vertical spine label; HOVER/FOCUS a slab and it EXPANDS to a near-full render of that component while the others compress to thin spines, its kicker + big serif label + material spec fading in. Move to the next slab and that one opens while the previous collapses - a smooth horizontal accordion flow. One open at a time. The owner's exact ask (big renders + hover the next one -> it opens), built ban-clean: the open is a clip-path inset + translateX, never a width/left/flex tween.

measured_teardown.move: Every slab is the SAME fixed full-rack-width layer stacked at the same origin (width:100% NEVER animated). JS computes a layout (the open slab takes openFlex of the rack, the rest split the remainder as equal strips, minus a px seam) and writes two CSS vars per slab: --x (left edge in % of rack -> transform: translateX) and --w (visible width in % of rack -> clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - --w) 0 0) showing only that band). CSS transitions --x (transform) and --w (clip-path) on the house air curve cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) ~620ms. Because the image is object-fit:cover, a strip shows a true vertical SLICE of the SAME render and the open slab shows the component near-full - no image swap, so no geometry jump: the slab you touch is the slab that opens. The spine label fades out / the bottom-left plate fades+rises in (delay .12s so the slab opens first). JS only computes the layout + toggles classes; the GPU does the motion.
measured_teardown.cited: ERA /architecture carouselSync + Springs 'Open the doors' clip-reveal grammar (a render strip handing off one component to the next) re-cast as a HOVER accordion: the seam that travels in those scroll engines becomes a clip-path inset that opens on hover, one slab at a time.

openFlex.what: the open slab's share of the rack width (0.4..0.82). 0.62 with 4 slabs => open ~62%, each of the 3 strips ~12.7% - a dominant open render with legible spines. Higher = more dominant open slab, thinner strips.

defaultIndex.what: which slab is open at rest (0..N-1), or -1 for an even resting row (no slab open). A non -1 default means the rack is never a flat dead row.

seam.what: px gap drawn between slabs, converted to a % of the rack and re-applied on resize (not a margin - it is folded into --x/--w so nothing layout animates).

ease.what: the open/collapse curve (the house 'air'). Applied to transform + clip-path + filter.

dur.what: seconds for the slab open/collapse (the content move).

uiDur.what: seconds for the spine-out / plate-in (the label move).

entry: LayerAccordionReveal.create(target, opts) -> { open(i), rest(), index, slabs, refresh, destroy }. target = the .lar-rack element. Pass panels:[{img,label,spec,kicker,alt}] and the engine BUILDS .lar-slab x N (each: .lar-shot img + .lar-spine + .lar-plate); or author the .lar-slab markup yourself and the engine reads it. On mouseenter/focusin/click/Enter a slab opens; mouseleave restores defaultIndex. Layout is computed in JS (px seam -> %, re-run on ResizeObserver) but ANIMATED purely via transform + clip-path.
law: transform (translateX) + clip-path (inset) + opacity + filter transition ONLY; width:100% on every slab is FIXED and never animated; NO width/height/top/left/margin/flex tween; NO mix-blend / NO backdrop-filter; NO WebGL; NO video.currentTime; will-change: transform, clip-path on the slabs (the moving layers), dropped to auto in the static fallback; keyboard parity (slabs are role=button, tabindex 0, Enter/Space open, aria-expanded tracks state); touch(hover:none)/reduced-motion -> a static labelled list (all slabs even, labels shown, no clip/transform transitions). owns_pin false, owns_scroll false (a hover/triggered primitive, not scroll).
gate_mode: triggered hover (not scroll). Verify: at rest one slab is open (~openFlex of the rack, plate shown) and the rest are strips with a vertical spine; hover/focus a strip -> it opens while the previous collapses (only ONE is_open at a time); the open slab's revealed render IS that component (Вінець=macro-roof, Пергола=macro-pergola, Фасад=day-34, Основа=aerial) and all four are visually distinct; leaving restores the default. Smoothness via the HOVER variant of the probe (arm the rAF meter, cycle hovers across all slabs) - NOT the wheel-scroll variant.
proven: lab: 4 slabs on OUR QUADRO renders. REST (defaultIndex 0): slab 0 open with --w ~62% + plate 'Вінець', slabs 1-3 strips ~12.7% with vertical spines. HOVER slab 3 -> --w opens to ~62% (Основа/aerial) while slab 0 collapses to a strip; only one .is-open at a time; aria-expanded follows. Each open render is a distinct component (rooftop deck / timber soffit / frontal facade / aerial site) - correspondence verified by clicking each slab in the probe and reading the painted render vs the plate label. Motion is transform+clip-path only (no layout property animates). Reduced-motion/touch -> static list, labels shown. window.__LAB_OK__ true, zero real console errors.
